title: Bident: Optical Logic Synthesis via Optimal Configuration of Binary-Combiner Trees
evidence_span: Bident models binary-tree topology and input ordering in multi-input optical combiners, uses Huffman optimization for Y-branch configuration and a greedy harmonic-mean strategy for directional couplers, and reports lower signal attenuation and switch cost with schematic-level optical simulation support.
problem: Existing optical logic synthesis uses oversimplified efficiency factors that omit physical attenuation and hierarchical signal degradation.
method_or_artifact: Binary aggregate loss model, Huffman tree optimization for Y-branch combiners, and greedy leaf-level directional-coupler configuration.
workload_or_benchmark: Optical logic synthesis and schematic-level optical circuit simulation; circuit sizes, technology, and logic workloads are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Photonic integrated circuits with binary-combiner trees, Y-branches, and directional couplers; loss parameters and fabrication assumptions are unspecified.
metrics: Superior signal-attenuation reduction and lower switch cost reported qualitatively
Harmonic-mean efficiency claimed for leaf couplers
limits: No numeric attenuation, switch count, energy, area, yield, or process results are supplied.
Schematic simulation does not establish fabricated photonic behavior or optical noise margins.
Official description only; comparisons require full-paper conditions.

title: CPW-SMO: Generating Mask Sets and Common Source for Maximum Common Process Window
evidence_span: CPW-SMO treats one-source-to-many-masks lithography optimization as a set-generation problem, using set attention, a parallel generative simulator, a CPW preference penalty, and an SMO-aware gradient response; the official description reports nearly 2x common process window and approximately 200x runtime speedup over state-of-the-art methods.
problem: Conventional source-mask optimization iteratively produces a single pair and does not efficiently co-optimize critical pattern sets under a common source.
method_or_artifact: Single-shot set-based generative source/mask optimization with attention, parallel simulation, preference-penalty scalarization, and SMO-aware gradients.
workload_or_benchmark: Full-chip or critical-pattern common-process-window lithography optimization; pattern sets, node, simulator, and mask constraints are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Advanced-node DTCO and source-mask optimization with common source and multiple masks; optical model, resist/process assumptions, and compute platform are unspecified.
limits: The description omits node, pattern count, process-window definition, fidelity constraints, and runtime hardware.
Speedup and CPW comparisons may depend on simulator fidelity and baseline stopping criteria.
Official description only; reported gains require paper-level verification.

title: From Fab to Mask Shop: A Differentiable MDP-ILT Framework for Co-Optimization of Wafer Pattern Fidelity and Mask Writability
evidence_span: The framework differentiates an electron-beam mask-data-preparation simulator using an error-function energy-deposition model, embeds optical-lithography simulation, and jointly optimizes shot parameters for wafer pattern fidelity and mask writability across the fab-to-mask-shop workflow.
problem: Disjoint inverse-lithography and mask-data-preparation workflows can optimize wafer fidelity and mask manufacturability inconsistently.
method_or_artifact: Physics-aware differentiable EBL simulation with exact gradients, optical-lithography simulation in the loop, and end-to-end shot-parameter co-optimization.
workload_or_benchmark: Curvilinear inverse-lithography and variable-shaped-beam mask preparation; pattern suite, process node, and shot counts are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Optical lithography and EBL mask-writing models with shot fracturing and geometry-level mask-process correction; process calibration and simulator settings are unspecified.
baselines: disjoint fab ILT and mask-shop MDP workflows
metrics: Improved mask manufacturability and preserved wafer pattern fidelity claimed qualitatively
limits: No numeric wafer error, writability, shot count, runtime, or process-window results are provided.
Differentiable simulator fidelity and calibration to physical EBL are unresolved.
Official description only; no independent fabrication or mask-write validation.

title: Agent-Per-Qubit: Automated Qubit Placement for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
evidence_span: QAgent assigns one reinforcement-learning agent to each logical qubit, jointly optimizes qubit layouts, and uses a Breakthrough Return Bonus to address sparse rewards and credit assignment; experiments on diverse quantum-circuit benchmarks report up to 53.9% lower execution cost and improved success rates, with ablations identifying BRB as important for stability.
problem: Logical-qubit placement is a hard compilation problem where traditional heuristics struggle to minimize execution cost on quantum processors.
method_or_artifact: Multi-agent reinforcement learning with one agent per logical qubit and dynamic Breakthrough Return Bonus reward shaping.
workload_or_benchmark: Diverse quantum-circuit placement benchmarks for fault-tolerant execution; processor topology, code, noise model, and circuit suite are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Quantum processor layout and fault-tolerant compilation with execution-cost and success-rate objectives; coupling graph, error rates, and routing model are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 53.9% reduction in execution cost
BRB identified as important in ablation
limits: The description omits circuit sizes, processor topology, noise/error model, training budget, and absolute costs.
Execution-cost and success-rate definitions and baseline tuning are unspecified.
Official description only; claims require paper-level and independent review.

title: FreqSEM: Frequency-Aware High-Precision Contour Extraction for Lithographic SEM Images
evidence_span: FreqSEM separates low- and mid-frequency SEM components with FFT, uses low-frequency structure to prompt SAM2 and mid-frequency detail in the encoder, and adds edge-aware and Sobel losses; with limited training data it reports EPE mean 0.334 nm and standard deviation 0.661 nm at an 81 nm minimum line width.
problem: Low contrast, noise, and complex structures in lithographic SEM images make precise contour extraction difficult for metrology and process optimization.
method_or_artifact: Frequency-aware FFT decomposition, SEM-adapted SAM2 prompting and feature injection, edge-weighted loss, and Sobel gradient loss.
workload_or_benchmark: Lithographic SEM contour extraction at an 81 nm minimum line width with limited training data; dataset, annotation, and cross-tool conditions are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: SEM-based lithographic metrology and image-analysis pipeline; imaging conditions, process node, pixel scale, and inference hardware are unspecified.
limits: No dataset size, annotation uncertainty, baseline values, runtime, or generalization across nodes is supplied.
Nanometer EPE depends on calibration and measurement conventions that are not described.
Official description only; metrology validity requires paper-level verification.
